summary: Margarita Iosifovna Vorobyova-Desyatovskaya studied at Saint Petersburg State University and the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts, working in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Central Asian studies. She served at the Institute of Oriental Studies (~1956–2021) and curated manuscripts there (1982–2005).
Margarita Kleibel is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Karin Preisendanz and completed her MA supervised by Klaus-Dieter Mathes.

Indologist Marguerite E. Adiceam studied at the University of Lyon and under Jean Filliozat. She taught at the Lycée Français de Pondichéry (1946–1954) and was a scientific member of the École française d'Extrême-Orient (1966–1971).

Marguerite Lobsiger-Dellenbach worked in history, archaeology, and Indology, earning her Ph.D. from the University of Geneva by 1935. She served as Vice-Director (1947) and Director (1952–1967) of the Musée d'ethnographie de Genève, succeeding Eugène Pittard.

Specializing in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology, Maria Carlotta Avanzi earned master's degrees from the University of Turin and a doctorate from Kyoto University. She was an associate professor at Akita Prefectural University (2021) and Italian School of East Asian Studies (attested 2026).

Maria Elisabeth Lulius van Goor studied under Jacob Samuel Speyer and earned her Ph.D. from Leiden University (1904–1915). Specializing in Indology and Buddhist studies, she was an attachée at EFEO (1922–1923) and Praeceptor of Pāli at Leiden (1924).

Maria Gallas works in philosophy and Indology. She completed a master's degree in philosophy at the National University of Distance Education (2019–2022) and is a PhD student at Universidad a Distancia de Madrid.

Maria Heim studied at Reed College and earned her PhD at Harvard University under Charles Hallisey, also studying under Jambuvijaya, W. S. Karunatillake, and Nagin J. Shah. She served as Associate Professor of Buddhist Studies at Amherst College (attested 2013–2020).

Maria Vasylieva earned degrees from Uppsala University, the National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine, Rangjung Yeshe Institute, and International Buddhist College. A specialist in Buddhist studies, she served as Assistant Professor at Rangjung Yeshe Institute in 2020.

Maria Wilkins Smith studied at Bryn Mawr College and earned her Ph.D. under Roland Grubb Kent at the University of Pennsylvania. Specializing in linguistics and Indology, she taught Latin at Temple University as Instructor and Assistant Professor (~1928–1952).

Marian Ury, a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies, completed her doctoral studies and PhD at the University of California, Berkeley. She served as professor of East Asian languages and comparative literature at the University of California, Davis (1969–1995).

Marianne Pieper studied at the Hamburger Hochschule für Wirtschaft und Politik and completed her habilitation at Otto von Guericke University Magdeburg. She held professorial positions at the University of Hamburg (1990–1994, 1996–2015) and the University of Kassel (1994–1996).

Marianne Winder studied at the University of London, University of Nottingham, UCL, and SOAS under David Llewellyn Snellgrove. Active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, she worked as Assistant Librarian, Curator, and Consultant in Tibetan Medicine at the Wellcome Trust.

Marianne Yaldiz is a scholar of archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. She served as Director of the Museum of Asian Art (attested 1997–2005) and Director of the Museum für Indische Kunst (attested 2006).

Mariano José Saldanha studied under Sebastião Rodolfo Dalgado and at several institutions in Goa and Lisbon. Active in Indology and linguistics, he taught at Liceu Nacional Afonso de Albuquerque (1915–1929), the University of Lisbon (1929–1946), and was Subdirector at ISCSP (1929–1948).

Mariano Rampolla del Tindaro studied under Oreste Nazari and at the Pontifical Gregorian University. Working in Indology, he was appointed professor of Indian religious history and Sanskrit at the Pontifical Urban University in 1933.
Marie Brožová was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. She studied at Charles University, completing her Ph.D. under the supervision of Josef Zubatý by 1921.
Marie G. Wanek worked in the fields of Indology and philosophy. She studied at the University of Pennsylvania under the instruction of Sengaku Mayeda.

Marie Gatellier was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Jean Boisselier and André Bareau. She held the post of Chargée de recherche at the National Centre for Scientific Research.

id: P:Marie-Jean-Léon Le Coq, Marquis d'Hervey de Saint-Denys
summary: Marie-Jean-Léon Le Coq, Marquis d'Hervey de Saint-Denys, was a Sinologist who studied under Stanislas Julien, whom he later succeeded. He also taught Édouard Chavannes.
